text:
support-alex: FYI - ACME on Dedicated pool 'acme-prod' opened a support ticket: sudden throughput drop ~50% since ~08:10 UTC, 429s for some spans. Customer says autoscale didn't add nodes. Can oncall triage?

maya: putting logs here from the customer's session and our pool metrics. quick note: they run a 8xA10x ondedicated with continuous-batcher + kv-cache enabled.

maya: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T08:09:52Z WARN batcher: scheduling delay=320ms queue_depth=42 max_batch_tokens=4096
2026-03-17T08:09:53Z ERROR throttle: tenant=acme-prod throttled=true reason=noisy_neighbor_estimate
2026-03-17T08:09:54Z INFO kvcache: miss_prefix=true key=conv:12345
2026-03-17T08:09:55Z WARN autoscale: scale_check=true active_nodes=6 target_nodes=6 cool_down=120s
```

maya: also attaching current pool config: `max_batch_tokens=4096`, `batch_window_ms=25`, `continuous_batcher.enabled=true`, `prefill_kv_cache=true`.

josh-oncall: thanks. first hypothesis: large `max_batch_tokens` with small `batch_window_ms` -> oversized candidate batches that get rejected late causing requeue thrashing and preventing autoscaler util signals. also noisy neighbor classifier flipped on and applied tenant-level throttle.

rachel-sre: can you confirm whether autoscaler uses queue_length or observed_gpu_util for scaling? if it's queue_length only, thrash might keep it pinned.

maya: autoscaler policy is `util_target=70%` with fallback to `queue_length>30` triggers; but recent change (deploy 2026-03-15) accidentally ignored `prefill_kv_cache` impact on effective tokens/sec.

infra-bot: Alert: noisy-tenant-detector fired for pool acme-prod (score=0.82) -> applied soft-throttle (60% cap) at 08:09:53 UTC.

josh-oncall: actionable repro steps for eng-runtime folks:
1) Run a synthetic traffic ramp against acme-prod with a mix of short & long sequences (mean tokens 600, p95 2800)
2) Capture batcher metrics: `rctl metrics get batcher --pool acme-prod --fields queue_depth,batch_size_histogram,pack_attempts,pack_rejects`
3) Check autoscaler logs: `rctl logs get autoscaler --pool acme-prod --since 10m`
4) Reproduce noisy_detector by spinning up a bursty tenant hitting long token sequences

maya: I ran step 2 and saw many `pack_rejects` spikes and high `pack_attempts` where attempted pack size > GPU capacity, then immediate requeues. that aligns with oversized `max_batch_tokens`.

rachel-sre: temporary mitigations we can push from control plane: 1) reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 2048 for acme-prod; 2) increase `batch_window_ms` to 45ms to give more time to fill fair smaller packs; 3) apply temporary noisy-tenant soft unthrottle while we stabilize so their SLA isn't impacted. Anyone object?

josh-oncall: +1 to tuning. note: reducing max_batch_tokens will increase token-per-request latency slightly but should reduce pack rejects and improve throughput. we should also flip on `kv_cache_prefill=true` for high reuse dialogs (customer already has it true but config mismatch reported).

maya: applied change in staging (repro env): `rctl pool update acme-prod --set max_batch_tokens=2048 --set batch_window_ms=45` and re-ran the ramp. results: pack_rejects dropped 90%, queue_depth median down from 42->8, observed throughput +38%. autoscaler now sees higher sustained util and scheduled +2 nodes (staging).

infra-bot: Config change recorded: change_id=chg-20260317-0992 approver=maya.

rachel-sre: long-term fix items: - avoid allowing `max_batch_tokens` so high by default for pools with mixed short/long seq workloads; - autoscaler should include `pack_reject_rate` as an input; - noisy-tenant detector to use smoothed metrics so transient pack rejects don't flip it. I'll open issues.

josh-oncall: immediate next steps for customer: 1) we'll roll the `max_batch_tokens`+`batch_window_ms` change to acme-prod canary 10% now; 2) keep noisy-detector soft-throttle disabled for them for 30m; 3) monitor for 15m and escalate to full rollback if failures.

support-alex: communicated plan to customer: canary change + expect throughput to recover within 10-15m, will follow up. They asked also whether their SDK call patterns (sending long context every request) could be tuned; recommended pooling state on client side and enabling kv-cache prefill for conversation reuse.

maya: leaving a quick reproduction snippet for eng folks to run locally against a canary pool (replace POOL and KEY):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "x-pool: $POOL" \
    -d '{"input":"'$(head -c 20000 /dev/urandom | base64)'"}' &
done
```
This produces mixed-sized requests and will trigger pack behavior.

rachel-sre: thanks all. I'll file two tickets and tag runtime-scheduler and autoscale squads. please add any logs to the ticket with correlating `trace_id` if you see requeues after change.

support-alex: customer acknowledged and appreciates the quick turnaround. closing the loop after 1h monitoring. :thumbsup:
